audio.note: Real ElevenLabs v3 take (voice UgBBYS2sOqTuMpoF3BR0), approved and locked. Every timestamp below comes from a local Whisper.cpp transcription of this exact file, reduced to sentence boundaries by scripts/sentence-timing.mts. No cut is hand-guessed.

treatment.structure: One continuous narrated video, not a silent sizzle plus a separate explained body. The approved VO speaks start to finish; every visual decision below is built to its real timing.
treatment.reference: Screen-forward primary: real captured UI and the real receipt are the hero, shown large and confidently. Paper-native accents only where they reinforce something true about the product, never generic shape motion graphics.
treatment.evidenceRule: Real capture supplies all interface behaviour, WebMCP calls, editing, preview, and the physical print. Visual treatment frames that evidence; it never covers or replaces it.
treatment.musicRule: Light instrumental jazz/lounge bed under the whole narration, ducked further under every sentence, never competing with speech. Licence recorded in assets/audio/music-license.md before this ships.

sequences.sentence: Let's say you're planning an upcoming trip.
sequences.visual: The agent host, prompt field empty or just starting. This is the frame the video opens on — VO begins at 0:00 under it, no silent pre-roll.
sequences.proof: Establishes the situation before any product UI is explained.

sequences.sentence: You tell your agent about it – you know, like Codex, OpenClaw, or Hermes – and you ask it to put together a list of everything you'll need to head out the door.
sequences.visual: The real prompt being typed and sent, in whichever single host is actually captured. The three names spoken are examples in the voiceover, not a requirement to show three different interfaces.
sequences.proof: Real typed prompt, real send action.
sequences.caution: The submission rules require the video to behave as it claims. Whichever agent is actually shown on screen should be one of the three named here.

sequences.sentence: OpenReceipt gives it real tools to make something for the real world: not just a text reply in the chat, but a beautiful, minimal, utilitarian to-go receipt.
sequences.visual: Cut to visible WebMCP tool activity firing (list_receipt_recipes / draft_receipt), then the first receipt blocks landing in the editor.
sequences.proof: list_receipt_recipes, draft_receipt — named tool calls, not a canned template.

sequences.sentence: Your agent can add a countdown, a packing list, even a surf forecast, all meticulously laid out and ready to read.
sequences.visual: The real Surfing Trip receipt finishing its draft: countdown, packing groups, surf forecast all visible. Punch in on the surf block specifically — it is the one WebMCP argument that needs no explanation once seen.
sequences.proof: draft_receipt result, the receipt built in video/assets/generated/surfing-trip.json.

sequences.sentence: Then, you can review the agent's first draft, edit it yourself, or ask your agent to change something in the copy.
sequences.visual: A real direct edit: click into a line, retype it by hand. This is the single most important shot in the film — it is what proves two hands on one document rather than a chatbot taking turns.
sequences.proof: A human editing the same document the agent just produced, live.

sequences.sentence: With WebMCP, you and your agent are working on the same shared canvas at the same time, so making edits is easy as can be.
sequences.visual: The agent's own edit_receipt call landing: one line changes, agent highlight and Undo visible, the rest of the document undisturbed.

sequences.sentence: When everything looks right, you get a preview of the exact receipt.
sequences.visual: preview_receipt response on screen with the real dot width and paper length — whatever the capture actually shows, not a placeholder number.

sequences.sentence: Then it's one button press to print, right from your own home thermal printer.
sequences.visual: Approve click on screen, match-cut to the real printer starting — macro on the motor, then pull back to the paper actually emerging.
sequences.proof: request_receipt_print approved, then the real print. This is the film's one match cut.

sequences.sentence: If you're feeling adventurous, you can even allow your agent to print completely on its own.
sequences.visual: Stay on the printer running — this is a four-second aside about a real settings toggle (printPolicy: "autonomous", src/state/storage.ts:13), not worth cutting away to a new screen for.
sequences.proof: A true, shipped feature, mentioned without a dedicated screen shot so pacing doesn't stall.

sequences.sentence: This same flow works for a grocery list, a morning brief, a reminder, meeting notes, anything that's more useful on physical paper than stuck in a digital chat.
sequences.visual: Quick montage proving breadth: the list_receipt_recipes catalogue (daily_brief, reminder, grocery_run, meeting_prep) or a few seconds scrolling the block library. Not a new demo — evidence that the surf trip is one instance of a general capability.
sequences.proof: The product's own recipe/block catalogue, real and already built.

sequences.sentence: OpenReceipt turns your ideas into something you can actually carry and use through the day.
sequences.visual: The torn receipt, then held or placed somewhere it's actually useful — board bag, by the door, on the dash.
sequences.proof: The physical payoff the whole film has been building to.

sequences.visual: Three short on-screen badges, one per phrase, timed to the words, over continued physical B-roll. No new screen needed — this is a list of facts, not a demo.
sequences.proof: Matches the repository's actual licence and architecture.

sequences.sentence: OpenReceipt. A printer your agent can reach.
sequences.visual: Wordmark and the existing approved tagline from content/site.json.
sequences.proof: Closes on the same line the product's own hero section uses.
